rows.grounds: ending with the son of the sun
a hundred thousand beyond the sun
the group of seven sages, and from that Dhruva likewise

items.question: How are the planetary and stellar distances measured from the earth upward?
premises: From the earth up to Saturn there is a group of five, each separated by a lakh.
The group of seven sages is a lakh beyond the sun.
Dhruva is likewise a lakh beyond the seven sages.
items.inference: The cosmic regions from earth through Saturn, the seven sages, and Dhruva are arranged in successive intervals of one lakh.
uncertainties: The exact unit of the lakh is not stated in this verse.
items.plain_english: The wise know that from the earth up to Saturn there are five, each at its own distance, and that the group of seven sages lies a lakh beyond the sun, and Dhruva likewise a lakh beyond them.

items.question: What is the nature and position of Dhruva in the cosmic order?
premises: Dhruva is Brahma himself in a lower form stationed in Brahma's place.
Dhruva is immovable and serves as the central pillar of the celestial mansions.
Dhruva stands above all those celestial mansions.
items.inference: Dhruva functions as the fixed axial support of the upper cosmic structure.
items.plain_english: Dhruva is Brahma himself in a lower form, immovable in Brahma's station. Having become the central pillar of all the celestial mansions, Dhruva stands above them all.

rows.grounds: all are to be understood as bound in the sphere of wind

items.question: What holds the heavenly regions together at the level of Dhruva?
premises: At this level all things are understood to be bound within the sphere of wind.
The seven heavenly wind-masses are present there.
These wind-masses begin chiefly with the cloud-bearing layer.
items.inference: The upper heavenly structure is supported and organized by seven principal strata of wind.
uncertainties: The names of all seven wind-masses are not listed in this verse.
items.plain_english: Here all things are to be understood as bound within the sphere of wind. The seven heavenly wind-masses are there, beginning chiefly with the cloud-bearing layer.

rows.grounds: they go to the heavenly world
according to the remainder of their merit

items.question: What happens to ritual performers who lack knowledge after reaching heaven?
premises: Those devoid of knowledge perform sacrifices and oblations and go to heaven.
Their stay in heaven ends when that merit is exhausted.
They return to the human world according to the remainder of their merit.
items.inference: Ritual merit without knowledge grants only a temporary ascent to heaven followed by return to the human world.
items.plain_english: Those who perform sacrifices and oblations but lack knowledge go from here to heaven; when that merit is exhausted, they return to the human world according to the merit that remains.

rows.grounds: from the earth up to Dhruva

items.question: What distances span the regions from earth to Dhruva and from heaven to Mahat?
premises: The distance from earth to Dhruva is given as fifteen lakhs.
The distance from heaven to Mahat is given as two crores and eighty-five lakhs.
These measures summarize the vertical extent of those cosmic regions.
items.inference: The text provides cumulative distance measures for the lower and middle cosmic spans.
uncertainties: The unit of measurement is implied but not explicitly named in this verse.
items.plain_english: Thus, from the earth up to Dhruva there are fifteen lakhs, and from heaven up to Mahat there are two crores and eighty-five lakhs.

rows.grounds: seers, sages, and perfected beings there
and those whose offices have ended

items.question: Who dwells in the world of Mahat?
premises: Seers, sages, and perfected beings such as Markandeya abide there.
Gods whose offices have been completed also dwell there.
Both groups are situated in the world of Mahat.
items.inference: Mahat is inhabited by accomplished beings and by gods who have finished their cosmic duties.
items.plain_english: In Mahat dwell seers, sages, and perfected beings such as Markandeya, and also gods whose offices have come to an end.

rows.grounds: in the intermediate region of Mahat
from the world of Mahat to Jana here

items.question: What lies between Mahat and Jana, and who inhabits Jana?
premises: In the interval of Mahat there are other beings who still enjoy their offices.
The distance from Mahat to Jana is eight crores.
Kapila and others dwell in Jana.
items.inference: The region between Mahat and Jana contains office-bearing beings, and Jana itself is inhabited by sages such as Kapila.
items.plain_english: In the interval of Mahat there are other beings who still hold their offices. From Mahat to Jana is eight crores, and there Kapila and others dwell.

rows.grounds: from Jana to Tapas is one crore here

items.question: Who dwells in Jana and what is the distance from Jana to Tapas?
premises: Many happy Sadhyas remain in Jana.
The distance from Jana to Tapas is one crore.
Sanaka and others of great intellect dwell in Tapas.
items.inference: Jana is a realm of blissful beings, while Tapas lies one crore above it and is inhabited by the great sages.
items.plain_english: Many happy Sadhyas remain there, and from Jana to Tapas is one crore; in Tapas dwell Sanaka and others of great wisdom.

items.question: What office is held in Tapas and how far is Satya from it?
premises: In Tapas the Prajapatis born from Brahma's own being hold their office.
Above Tapas lies Satya, the abode of Brahma.
The distance from Tapas to Satya is sixteen crores.
items.inference: Tapas is the domain of Brahma-born Prajapatis, and Satya lies far above it as Brahma's abode.
items.plain_english: There the Prajapatis born from Brahma's own being hold their office. Above Tapas, at a distance of sixteen crores, is Satya, the abode of Brahma.

rows.grounds: the self-born one manifests this universe

items.question: What takes place in the world of Satya?
premises: The self-born Brahma abides in Satya and manifests this universe.
The Vedas and others are present in Satya.
They are cultivated there through ritual action and meditation.
items.inference: Satya is the realm where Brahma manifests the universe and where Vedic realization is perfected through action and meditation.
items.plain_english: There the self-born Brahma abides and manifests this universe. In Satya the Vedas and others are cultivated through ritual action and meditation.

rows.grounds: those established in bliss are there, and one crore above is the seat of Brahma
two crores from the seat of Brahma
is described as belonging to Vishnu

items.question: What regions lie above Satya in relation to Brahma and Vishnu?
premises: Beings established in bliss dwell above Satya.
One crore above is the seat of Brahma.
Two crores beyond Brahma's seat is the city of Vishnu.
items.inference: The cosmology ascends in measured stages from Satya to Brahma's seat and then to Vishnu's city.
uncertainties: The compound in the first token is compressed and its exact segmentation is interpretive.
items.plain_english: Those established in bliss dwell there, and one crore above is the seat of Brahma; two crores beyond Brahma's seat is described as the city of Vishnu.

rows.grounds: devotees of Vishnu through meditation, worship, and recitation
seven crores beyond the world of Vishnu is the world

items.question: How do devotees reach Vishnu's abode and what lies beyond it?
premises: Devotees of Vishnu reach his abode through meditation, worship, and recitation.
Beyond the world of Vishnu lies another world.
That higher world is seven crores beyond and belongs to the supreme lord.
items.inference: Devotional practice leads to Vishnu's realm, which is still below the world of the supreme lord Rudra.
items.plain_english: Devotees of Vishnu reach his abode through meditation, worship, and recitation; seven crores beyond the world of Vishnu is the world of the supreme lord.

rows.grounds: of the maker of creation and dissolution within the path of the cosmic egg
intent on worship of the linga

items.question: Which worshippers are being described in relation to Rudra's world?
premises: Rudra is the lord of creation and dissolution within the cosmic egg.
Some worshippers are devoted to linga worship.
Those worshippers lack initiation and knowledge.
items.inference: The verse distinguishes linga devotees without initiation and knowledge as a specific class of aspirants to Rudra's realm.
items.plain_english: This refers to those who, within the realm of the cosmic egg, are devoted to the worship of Rudra's linga but lack initiation and knowledge, though Rudra is the lord of creation and dissolution.

items.question: What is the destiny of those who reach Rudra's city within the cosmic egg?
premises: The previously described worshippers go to Rudra's city within the cosmic egg.
They never fall downward from there.
All who dwell there eventually go to Shiva as Rudras initiated by Srikantha.
items.inference: Rudra's city is a non-regressive stage from which its inhabitants ultimately attain Shiva.
items.plain_english: They go to Rudra's city within the cosmic egg and never fall downward again. All who dwell there become Rudras initiated by Srikantha and go to Shiva.

rows.grounds: when their office comes to an end
with the host of Rudra's daughters
above Rudra in ever higher succession

items.question: What happens to the Rudras when their office ends?
premises: The Rudras' office eventually comes to an end.
They move onward together with the host of Rudra's daughters.
They ascend from city to city above Rudra in successive stages.
items.inference: Even after completing their office, the Rudras continue an upward progression through higher realms.
items.plain_english: When their office ends, they go on together with the host of Rudra's daughters, ascending from city to city above Rudra in ever higher succession.

items.question: What is the role of Dandapani in relation to the cosmic egg and liberation?
premises: Below the cosmic egg and above Rudra is the city of Dandapani.
By Shiva's will Dandapani strengthens the cosmic egg.
He also makes the path of liberation.
items.inference: Dandapani serves as a stabilizing guardian of the cosmic structure and as an agent of the path to liberation.
items.plain_english: Below the cosmic egg and above Rudra is the city of Dandapani. By Shiva's will he strengthens the cosmic egg and also opens the path of liberation.

items.question: Who are the seven world-lords presiding from the earth world upward?
premises: The verse names Sharva, Rudra, Bhima, Bhava, Ugra, Mahan, and Ishana.
These seven are described as lords of the worlds.
They preside from the earth world upward as forms of Shiva.
items.inference: The cosmic hierarchy is governed by seven Shiva-forms acting as world-lords.
uncertainties: The exact mapping of each lord to each world is not specified in this verse.
items.plain_english: Sharva, Rudra, Bhima, Bhava, Ugra, Mahan, and Ishana are the seven lords of the worlds, forms of Shiva presiding from the earth world upward.

items.question: How are the seven worlds and the higher worlds constituted according to the teacher?
premises: Seven worlds are constituted by gross particular elements.
The higher worlds are constituted by subtle elements.
The teacher explained this properly in the Ruru scripture.
items.inference: The cosmic worlds are arranged by a gradation from gross to subtle constitution.
items.plain_english: The seven worlds are formed from gross particular elements, while the higher worlds are formed from subtle ones; the teacher explained this clearly in the Ruru scripture.

rows.grounds: in the first creation by Brahma

items.question: What are the gross particulars from which the lower worlds arise?
premises: In Brahma's first creation certain elements were fashioned from his own body.
These are called the abundant gross particulars and are five in number.
The worlds are made of them, with a seventh principle consisting of them.
items.inference: The lower worlds are grounded in five gross particular elements produced in Brahma's primordial creation.
uncertainties: The identity of the seventh principle is compressed in the verse and not fully explicit.
items.plain_english: In Brahma's first creation, five gross particular elements, called the abundant ones, were fashioned from his own body; the worlds are made of them, with a seventh principle consisting of them.

rows.grounds: by subtle great elements born of the tanmatras
having supported them by the coverings of the worlds
by smell and the other subtle qualities

items.question: How are the higher worlds supported beyond the gross elements?
premises: Beyond the gross elements there are subtle supports.
These supports are subtle great elements born of the tanmatras.
They uphold the worlds as coverings through mutual relations of smell and the other subtle qualities.
items.inference: The higher worlds are structured by subtle tanmatric elements functioning as interrelated coverings.
uncertainties: The syntax is compressed, so the exact force of 'liṅgādhāraiḥ' is somewhat interpretive.
items.plain_english: Beyond those, the worlds are supported by subtle great elements born of the tanmatras, which act as coverings and are mutually connected through smell and the other subtle qualities.

rows.grounds: from Kalagni up to Dandapani there are ninety-eight crores
the shell of the cosmic egg

items.question: What is the extent from Kalagni to Dandapani and what lies above it?
premises: The span from Kalagni to Dandapani is ninety-eight crores.
Above that lies the shell of the cosmic egg.
That shell is dense and one crore yojanas thick.
items.inference: The cosmic egg is bounded above Dandapani by a massive solid shell of defined thickness.
uncertainties: The unit for the ninety-eight crores is not explicitly stated in this verse.
items.plain_english: From Kalagni up to Dandapani there are ninety-eight crores; above that, in the cosmic egg, is its shell, dense and a crore yojanas thick.

rows.grounds: downward from the surface of the earth
from that comes the golden grain

items.question: What is the total vertical extent of the earth and what lies beyond it?
premises: The earth extends fifty crores upward from its surface.
It extends fifty crores downward as well.
Thus the earth totals a hundred crores, beyond which is the golden grain.
items.inference: The earth is conceived as a vast hundred-crore structure bounded beyond by the golden grain.
uncertainties: The term 'golden grain' is metaphorical in this verse and its cosmological referent is not fully explained.
items.plain_english: The earth extends fifty crores upward from its surface and fifty crores downward, making a hundred crores in all; beyond that is the golden grain.

rows.grounds: extending up to the hundred Rudras, with the sound huphut

items.question: How is the region of the hundred Rudras described around the cosmic structure?
premises: The boundary extends up to the hundred Rudras and is marked by the sound huphut.
That region is hard to pierce or subdue.
Ten Rudras in each direction make a hundred Rudras outside.
items.inference: The outer boundary is guarded by a formidable array of a hundred Rudras distributed in all directions.
uncertainties: The ritual or sonic force of 'huphaṭ' is indicated but not explained in this verse.
items.plain_english: Up to the hundred Rudras, marked by the sound huphut, that hard-to-subdue boundary must be pierced; with ten in each direction, there are a hundred Rudras outside.

rows.grounds: having the nature of the egg
in the Raurava and other scriptures

items.question: What supports the cosmic egg and how is that support described by the teachers?
premises: There is a support of the cosmic egg.
It supports the egg on all sides by its own inherent power.
The teachers in the Raurava and other scriptures describe it as having the nature of the egg.
items.inference: The cosmic egg is upheld by a self-powered support that is itself egg-like in nature, according to authoritative teachers.
items.plain_english: That which supports the cosmic egg does so on all sides by its own power; the teachers in the Raurava and other scriptures declare it to be of the same nature as the egg.
